text:
sre-bot: :rotating_light: 2429998888 ALERT: kv-cache eviction rate x15 over baseline, continuous-batching queue length growing, correlated with prefetcher spike for models: mistral-2, qwen-7b, llama-70b. 5xx rate increased from 0.2% -> 4.3% in last 2m. Auto-mitigation: canary fallback not triggered.

maya: I'm on it. Pulling logs, joining now. paging @oncall.

oncall: I've muted non-critical alerts. Can someone confirm customer-facing latency SLO violations?

mei: Monitoring shows tail latency > 1.2s for embed+gen routes for a subset of requests, error budget creeping. A few mid-market accounts saw anomalous error spikes (acct: fin-ops, acct:searchlytics). Notified CS.

raj: Root signal looks like prefetcher increased prefix fanout when MQA fallback turned on during a model switch earlier today. Prefetch spawned many long KV preloads; that pushed many shards into eviction loops under cont-batch aggregator.

sam: Paging infra: eviction pressure -> excessive async writes -> IO backpressure -> request handlers blocked -> request timeouts. I can throttle prefetchers at the routing layer. Do we want an immediate kill or soft throttle?

maya: Soft throttle first: reduce prefetch concurrency to 1 per request and cap prefetch TTL to 10s. If no improvement in 60s, escalate to full disable.

raj: Agreed. Applying routing flag now.

raj: ```bash
# soft throttle via config API
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OP'
  https://config-api.internal/v1/flags/prefetch -d '{"concurrency":1,"ttl_s":10}'
```

raj: Patch applied. Monitoring...

sre-bot: 2429998954 METRIC: eviction_rate down 40% after flag flip, cont-batch queue length decreased ~30%, 5xxs trending down to 1.8%.

mei: Good. CS reported immediate reduction in errors for Searchlytics but Fin-Ops still sees intermittent spikes.

sam: Noted a second pathological path: for llama-70b we still see large prefix KV entries causing compaction storms. Can we apply model-specific prefetch blacklist for llama-70b?

maya: Yes, add llama-70b to no-prefetch list and limit MQA fanout for qwen. Raj, can you deploy that rule?

raj: Doing per-model rules now. ```json
{"rules": [{"model":"llama-70b","prefetch":false},{"model":"qwen-7b","mqa_fanout_max":3}]}
```

raj: Rules pushed at 2429999020.

sre-bot: 2429999026 METRIC: error rate down to 0.9%, eviction rate further down. Latency p50 back to baseline, p95 still ~1.05s.

cs-lead: CS update: notified both customers with ETA for root cause investigation. They're asking if this was a code change or a bad rollout. Can we confirm?

raj: Short answer: rollout of a heuristic tweak to cont-batch aggressiveness + enabling an MQA fallback for a canary caused synergistic growth in prefetch fanout. Combined with a shard imbalance, it multiplied evictions. Not a hardware issue.

mei: I'll draft a customer-facing note: explain mitigation, ETA for root cause, and whether any data loss occurred (none expected).

oncall: Live mitigation checklist — what's still open?

maya: Open tasks: 1) Observe stability for 30m after per-model rules (in progress). 2) Run offline sim against cont-batch heuristic with current workload. 3) Schedule rollback of heuristic change if we reproduce in staging. 4) Postmortem owner assignment.

sam: Also, we should consider a short-term config to lower max_batch_size globally from 64 -> 32 to reduce KV churn. That will reduce throughput but protects stability.

oncall: Approve lower max_batch_size to 32. Please apply and monitor.

raj: Applying global batch cap now. ```bash
kubectl exec -it config-updater -- curl -X POST
  localhost:8080/v1/runtime-config -d '{"max_batch_size":32}'
```

sre-bot: 2429999201 METRIC: max_batch_size change active. p95 latency decreased to 0.9s, throughput -18% as expected. Error rate stable ~0.5%.

cs-lead: Sending update to affected customers: short mitigation deployed, latencies improved, temporary throughput reduction may affect peak windows. Will update when root cause postmortem is ready.

maya: Confirming the immediate incident is mitigated. Will maintain watch for two more 15m windows. If stable, we'll hand off to next shift.

sam: Noted one lingering item: background compaction tasks queued on shard-43 are taking longer — will increase IO budget on that node to clear backlog. Doing now.

sre-bot: 2429999440 METRIC: shard-43 compactions processing, backlog reducing.

mei: For the postmortem, propose owners: raj (runtime), sam (infra), maya (oncall), mei (product/CS). Assign severity P1->P2 for follow-up since customer impact limited after mitigation.

oncall: I'll take the handoff. Summary for next oncall: prefetch heuristic + MQA fallback triggered cross-model prefetch storm, mitigated by throttling prefetch, per-model no-prefetch rule (llama-70b), mqa fanout cap for qwen-7b, and global max_batch_size reduction to 32. Remaining work: reproduce in staging, root-cause postmortem, consider reverting heuristic change or adding safety caps.

oncall: Handoff to night oncall @raj_night at 2429999608 — full notes in ops-runbook. 

raj: Ack — will monitor overnight. If any regression, revert to pre-change config and open rollback PR.

cs-lead: Thanks team. I'll follow up with customers in 2 hours with an incident summary and next steps. :thumbsup:
